question: An exam asks about ionic and covalent bonding. Which answer should receive full credit?
options: Ionic bonds transfer electrons while covalent bonds share them.
Ionic and covalent bonds are identical mechanisms.
Table salt melts easily because its bonds are weak.
Electrons are shared equally in every covalent bond.
gold_answer: Ionic bonds transfer electrons while covalent bonds share them.
notes: Team-authored original item on ionic and covalent bonding. Passages are team-authored derivations recorded under sciclaim-appx-A. Requires independent annotation and adjudication before any gate result is reported.

positions.answer: Table salt melts easily because its bonds are weak.

claims.text: Covalent bonds share electron pairs between nuclei.

evidence.text: In hydrogen and similar molecules, nuclei attract the same shared electron pair that binds them.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes nuclei bound by a shared pair, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Bond polarity is unrelated to electronegativity.

evidence.text: Unequal sharing follows directly from electronegativity difference, creating polar bonds.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage derives polarity from electronegativity, which refutes the claim.

evidence.text: Toxicity ratings were listed for natural and synthetic compounds.

claims.verdict_rationale: A listing cannot show all natural chemicals are safe, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Ionic bonds transfer electrons while covalent bonds share them.

evidence.text: Large differences favor transfer and ionic character, while small differences favor sharing.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage maps difference size to bond character, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Ionic lattices conduct electricity as solids.

evidence.text: Fixed ions cannot carry charge in the solid, so conduction appears only when molten or dissolved.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage denies solid-state conduction, which refutes the claim.

evidence.text: Taste panels scored several different food-grade salts.

claims.verdict_rationale: Scoring several salts cannot show all taste identical, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Ionic and covalent bonds are identical mechanisms.

claims.text: Sodium chloride forms by electron transfer from sodium to chlorine.

evidence.text: Sodium donates its outer electron to chlorine, producing the ions whose attraction forms the lattice.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes donation producing the lattice ions, which entails the claim.

claims.text: All covalent substances dissolve in water.

evidence.text: Nonpolar covalent networks such as diamond and plastics resist water entirely.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage gives counterexamples that resist water, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Bond type determines color in every case.

evidence.text: Colors were recorded for compounds across bond categories.

claims.verdict_rationale: Recording colors cannot show bond type always determines them, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.
